exposition: Section 3 gives the certificate acceptance test, failure-triggered refinement, and the finite comparison horizon. Section 4 retains the remaining-order count and affine cost interface, proving the asymptotic fixed-stage bound without the ancillary +17 coefficient. Section 5 first states when certification must succeed, then proves the anchor gain in both branches. Section 6 uses a gap bound for every pair, including comparable coordinates. Section 7 bounds refinements by n Q(n) and precision by P log E. Appendix B uses a conditional-moment averaging lemma. The abstract, disclosure, related work, and existing figures are unchanged; Sections 1 and 3 change only as required by the algorithm and roadmap.

source_material: Latest completed assistant message in Simplify Paper Arguments, retrieved through the connected chat reader. The 20,000-character response contains all six technical proposals and truncates the final summary paragraph. The linked PDF and source archive were not downloaded. implementation_change: Certify always computes two lower fractions; the comparison rule refines only if neither meets 1/2-eta, after the existing path and degree checks. ChooseAnchor first tries CentralInterval and otherwise uses the effective interval middle half. The width scale is used only in calibration and proofs. After Q(n)=n ceil(log2(n)) answers the algorithm switches to a consistent fixed order. The locality parameters use exact rational tests for a moment power and number of sweeps. Precision is at most P log E, with P at most n Q(n).
